title: P39-family stochastic depth: per-sample drop-path 0.1 on the 12 residual branches of the six Peri-LN trunk blocks during pretraining only (off at handoff), on the 151-claude width-320 Lean incumbent
description: Idea ID: P39-family (pretraining-only residual-branch regularizer, removed at handoff); the mechanism is stochastic depth (Huang et al. 2016; LayerDrop, Fan et al. 2020), never tried in either protocol (050-codex tried 5% residual dropout and 128-claude 0.1 attention-probability dropout, both under recipes that did not overfit). pretrain.py is 151-claude's except that in every training forward each of the 12 residual writes of the six trunk blocks is zeroed for an independent random 10% of the samples and the kept writes are scaled by 1/0.9; the MTP block, the val pass and the handed-off model run all branches (drop_path reset to 0 on every block before return, since the frozen RL stage calls train()). Since 148 the token-batch recipe runs 4-5 epochs and memorizes the 155k-record cap-6 set (148: train 0.03 vs val 0.088, val minimum at 90-195 s then rising; 151: minima 0.074-0.081 at 75-285 s, final 0.083-0.088, train ~0.04-0.06), and 148 handed RL a worse round-1 sampler (273/408/264 targets vs 136's 577/529/662; round-1 Lean parse failures 57/52/51% vs 44/48/34%); 150 (bigram table) and 151 (width, kept +13.7) spend the surplus on capacity, this one spends it on regularization of the now-larger 7.47M trunk: a trunk trained to give the right next token when any of its 12 writes is missing keeps smoother, more redundant proof-state features, which should sample better at T=0.8 on out-of-distribution length >= 7 targets and give expert iteration a better start.
hypothesis: Mechanism: at ~4.4 epochs the 7.47M-param trunk fits individual training proofs (train CE ~0.04-0.06, val ~0.085 and rising after its minimum) with sharp, co-adapted per-block writes; 148's val rise and round-1 sampler collapse are the symptoms, and 151's larger trunk has more room to memorize. Per-sample drop-path is dropout at the granularity of a residual write: every step trains a random sub-network of the 12 writes (2^12 members, expected 10.8 active), so no single write can carry a memorized detail and the ensemble-like averaging at handoff is smoother; unlike unit dropout it never perturbs the token/position identity inside a branch, so the exact-symbol precision a proof needs is kept. Measured cost is nil (bench on the 256-wide tree: 13.03 vs 13.2 steps/s; sampling 192 vs 186 samples/s), so the comparison is at equal steps and epochs. Predictions, in order of confidence: (1) pretraining steps 4,200-5,300 per seed (151: 5003/4900/4375), epochs 3.7-4.7; (2) train loss (main CE, measured under the drop) ends at 0.05-0.08, above 151's 0.042-0.062; (3) the val curve's minimum comes later (>= 135 s on every seed; 151: 135/285/75 s) and the final val loss is 0.076-0.086 with a final-minus-minimum rise under 0.005 on every seed (151: final 0.085/0.083/0.088, rises 0.004/0.007/0.014); (4) held-out greedy after pretraining 0.93-0.97 (151: 0.956/0.9325/0.9625); (5) the main mechanistic claim: round-1 RL targets solved 380-750 with the 3-seed mean above 151's 432 (151: 680/237/378; 148: 273/408/264), round-1 Lean parse failures 35-50% (148: 57/52/51%); (6) metric 640-715, central 684 (+12), keep needs > 672.33; totals 1,500-1,750 s as 151 (same model and sampling speed, no timeout risk). Falsifiers: round-1 targets solved mean <= 432 means the regularizer did not repair the sampler (then the round-1 variance is seed noise or a data-order effect of length-homogeneous batches, 002's reading, not overfitting); final val loss above 151's on every seed means p 0.1 underfits this trunk in 300 s (then the recipe is still capacity-limited, 151's reading, and a smaller p or none is right); a better sampler with an unchanged metric (as 148 vs 136) means RL repairs the sampler anyway and the score is set elsewhere.
expected_delta: -30 to +45 theorems at >=7 (3-seed mean), central +12; keep needs > 672.33. Mechanism: round-1 RL targets solved 380-750 with mean above 151's 432, pretraining steps 4,200-5,300 per seed, final val loss 0.076-0.086 with a final-minus-minimum rise under 0.005

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) ALiBiGPT with Peri-LN blocks and hybrid ALiBi/NoPE heads, unchanged from 151-claude (d_model 320); PeriLNBlock.forward now routes each branch output through residual(), a per-sample stochastic-depth mask that is the identity when drop_path is 0 or the block is in eval (CPU check at width 320: after the handoff reset the train-mode forward equals the eval forward exactly, 0.0 max abs diff)
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope (unchanged from 115-fable): no rotation of q/k in any block; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query position - key position) on the scaled attention logits via SDPA attn_mask, slopes 2^(-8h/4) = 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256 for heads 1..4 (Press et al. 2021 standard set for 4 heads) and 0 for heads 5..8 (bias identically 0 except -inf for masked/future keys, i.e. NoPE heads); same slope table in every block; -inf for masked/future keys
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: vs 151-claude: stochastic depth (Huang et al. 2016; LayerDrop, Fan et al. 2020) with p = 0.1 on the 12 residual branches of the six trunk blocks during pretraining only. Same ALiBiGPT (6 Peri-LN blocks of width 320, 8 heads of 40, d_ff 1280, hybrid ALiBi/NoPE heads, 7,474,560 params), same pretraining-only MTP module (its block is NOT dropped), same loss, optimizers, schedule, init, token-budget batches and handoff. The handed-off model is architecturally identical to 151-claude's: every block runs every branch.
arch.n_params_detail: model: identical to 151-claude, 7,474,560 (vocab 107; CPU check model.n_params() == 7,474,560 before and after pretrain()). MTP module (pretraining only, not on the model): 1,440,320 as in 151-claude; drop-path adds no parameters; pretraining trains 8,914,880 in total, under the 10M cap even if counted
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 320, 8) from this pretrain.py with PeriLNBlock blocks (drop_path 0), then load state: same keys and same function as 151-claude. The MTP module is not saved and is not needed for inference
arch.kv_cache: unchanged from 151-claude (caches[0] holds key positions); CPU check cached vs full forward max abs logit diff 1.3e-6 at width 320 with drop_path 0

drop_path.granularity: per sample (B,1,1 mask) and per residual branch: 12 independent Bernoulli(0.1) draws per sample per training forward (attention write and MLP write of each of the six trunk blocks)
drop_path.scaling: kept branch outputs multiplied by 1/(1-p) = 1.111 during pretraining so the expected residual write is unchanged; nothing is rescaled at handoff
drop_path.active: pretraining training forwards only (the val pass runs model.eval(); the MTP module's block keeps the class default 0 and is never dropped); pretrain() sets drop_path = 0.0 on every trunk block before returning because the frozen RL stage calls model.train()
drop_path.rng: torch.rand on the default CUDA generator (harness torch.manual_seed(seed)); the batch/shift generator `gen` is untouched, so batch order and name shifts are identical to 151-claude at the same seed
drop_path.cost: one (B,1,1) multiply per branch. bench_pretrain.py was run on this edit over the 256-wide 148 tree before 151's keep landed: 13.03 steps/s over 60 s (785 steps) vs 148-fable's 13.2, 5.28 GB peak, 192 samples/s sampling, i.e. no measurable cost; not re-benched at width 320 (same op), 151's own 5003/4900/4375 steps are the throughput reference

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 078-claude except the orthogonalization polynomial); the MTP module's five 2D matrices (block qkv split into Q/K/V, block proj, fc1, fc2, and the (256,512) input proj) join the Muon group and its LayerNorm gains/biases and projection biases join AdamW, same lr, schedule and decay as the trunk
optimizer.schedule: cosine over wall-clock with CHANGED floor: after the 200-step linear warmup, lr = 1e-3 * (0.3 + 0.35 * (1 + cos(pi * frac))), frac = elapsed / budget, ending at 0.3 x peak (115-fable: 0.1 x peak). Muon lr = 0.01 * lr / 1e-3 follows the same factor, and so does its per-step decoupled decay lr * MUON_WD

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / D) with D = 320 per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 2, head (107,320) 1, MTP proj (320,640) sqrt(2); same ratios as 148, MUON_LR 0.01 unchanged (Muon's spectral-norm step transfers across width for square matrices)
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW (floor CHANGED 0.1 -> 0.3); muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: 6 x (qkv.weight (960,320) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight, plus the MTP module's 5 matrices: 30 Muon matrices as in 148
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: unchanged: each QKV update reshaped to (3,320,320), orthogonalized per role
muon.coefficients_note: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, + ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. The new output-LayerNorm gains and biases get the same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as every other LayerNorm
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale. Because decay is lr-scaled, the higher floor raises late-training per-step decay (endpoint 3x 115's); MUON_WD itself is unchanged at 0.1
optimizer.clipping: unchanged: joint global gradient norm 1.0 over model.parameters() + the MTP module's parameters, before both optimizers (gradients are those of the stochastic-depth forward)
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; the MTP module and both pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW on model.parameters()
optimizer.parameters: 129's 24 hidden matrices + head.weight, plus the MTP module's qkv (split), proj, fc1, fc2 and input proj (256,512; RMS shape scale sqrt(2)): 30 Muon matrices during pretraining; the handoff model's parameters are unchanged

batch.padding: to max len in batch (the batch's last, longest record); mean padded tokens per step ~18.3k of which ~18.3k real (>99% fill), vs the incumbent's ~51-54k padded slots for ~17.3k real tokens
batch.change: fairseq-style max-tokens batching replaces fixed 128 random records per step: per epoch, randperm the training records (GPU generator, seed), stable-argsort by total length so equal lengths stay shuffled, cut greedily into consecutive runs with count * max_len <= 18,432, then shuffle the run order with random.Random(seed). Loss is the same per-token mean over the batch's proof tokens; the shift augmentation, Muon/AdamW updates, warmup, clip and wall-clock cosine are unchanged. The val slice still uses fixed chunks of 128.
batch.size_note: variable: a run of length-sorted records with count * padded_length <= TOK_BUDGET = 18,432 tokens (128 x 144); on a synthetic length distribution matching mean ~135 / max 537 that is 33..921 records per batch, mean ~136, so ~1,130 batches per epoch (incumbent: 128 fixed, ~1,204 per epoch)

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)
data.order: shuffle at the record level each epoch, then length-homogeneous batches in shuffled order (data-order change: within a step all records have similar total length; across steps lengths are interleaved at random)

config.init: unchanged rule from 148: fork _init (normal 0.02 embedding/readout, zero biases), orthogonal_ on every 2D block and MTP parameter with gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols)), so element std stays 0.02 at width 320; LayerNorm gain 1, bias 0

loss.main: the fork's loss_on: next-token cross-entropy on proof-token positions (unchanged; val_loss and the recorded train_loss/last_loss use this term only, so they stay comparable with 129)
loss.mtp: DeepSeek-V3 (2024) sequential multi-token prediction, depth 1 (Gloeckle et al. 2024 style shared head): z_t = proj(cat(LN(h_t), LN(emb(x_{t+1})))) for t in 0..T-3, one Peri-LN causal block over z with the same ALiBi/NoPE bias sliced to T-2 positions, then the model's ln_f and head predict x_{t+2}; cross-entropy masked to proof-token targets (m[:, 2:]), mean over those positions
loss.total: main + MTP_WEIGHT * mtp with MTP_WEIGHT = 0.3 constant over the whole budget (DeepSeek-V3's early-training value); curve points also record the mean recent mtp loss as mtp_loss
loss.leakage_check: CPU check: perturbing token x[7] changes the MTP block's outputs only at positions 6..9 (which read emb(x[7]) or later), never at position 5 whose target is x[7]

regularization.pretraining_only: stochastic depth p 0.1 per sample per residual branch on the six trunk blocks (see arch.drop_path); disabled before handoff
regularization.persisting_into_rl: none (weight decay conventions unchanged; RL uses the frozen harness AdamW)
